lines.text_table: [The light... it was around me, then in me. I was blinded by it. It was so bright. It was under my skin, glowing within my muscles. Lighting up my brain. It sliced me up, moved things around, discarded parts of me, replicated others. I don’t understand any of this. I don’t understand why this happened. It didn’t hurt. It felt like things were clicking into place, but not for me, for something else. And then... it wasn’t enough; whatever it needed me to be, whatever its purpose was, I wasn’t enough. It changed me, but it didn’t change me all the way. It just left me. And then... the light went away. I was left in the dark. It’s quiet and calm and I feel like... I can rest here.]

lines.text_table: Pain. Always pain. My feet aching, my muscles sore. Again, again, again. Pain builds muscle memory. Enough repetition, and it’s smooth. I don’t have to think about it anymore. It’s in my bones: the flow, the movement. The Pattern. And then the pain goes away, pushed down to where it doesn’t matter anymore. In its place, a poetry of motion, just me and the kinetic pleasure, like I become fluid, unrestricted. And afterwards: the pain now a pleasant ache of satisfaction, of completeness. I’ll never have that again. No bones, no muscles. No movement. I’m still. I’m so still.

lines.text_table: [I let it change me. I let it change me. I let it change me. I let it change me. I let it change me. I let it change me. Did I? Didn't I? Everyone changes for the worse. Maybe not. Faden changed. Was he better? I couldn't see it. Didn't want to. Look at me now. Is it my fault? Couldn't control it. Didn't. Thought I was helping. Thought it was good. The light... The Patterning... I couldn't shut it out. Didn't know it was already in. Inside me. How long? It wasn't me, was it? Why did I do it? Did I let it in? It's over now. At least it's over now. No more fighting. No more failing. I'm so sorry.]

options.text: You're making things harder out here
You have a unique way of speaking

lines.text_table: Hello? What is this place--
lines.text: Hello? What is this place--
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-2.99]This is my fortress, my port in the storm. [3.09-5.68]I built it with my very own hands!
lines.text: This is my fortress, my port in the storm. I built it with my very own hands!
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: It's a bunker.
lines.text: It's a bunker.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: [0-3.04]O-kay... I'm with the government. [3.25-5.21]We can evacuate you to a safe place.
lines.text: O-kay... I'm with the government. We can evacuate you to a safe place.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: One must be ready for anything -- this is what I've been preparing for all my life.
lines.text: One must be ready for anything -- this is what I've been preparing for all my life.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: You're making things harder out here for the people trying to help.
lines.text: You're making things harder out here for the people trying to help.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: A lot harder...
lines.text: A lot harder...
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: My meaning is not to harm innocents, though. Just the...
lines.text: My meaning is not to harm innocents, though. Just the...
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: [0-1.59]...the ones that are coming. [2.35-5.05]It's either me or them!
lines.text: ...the ones that are coming. It's either me or them!
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: Is there anyone in there with you?
lines.text: Is there anyone in there with you?
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: Only I. Some people came knocking at my door, offering the very thing you're trying to tempt me with.
lines.text: Only I. Some people came knocking at my door, offering the very thing you're trying to tempt me with.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: I could see them from my surveillance monitors, getting slaughtered by those... unearthly monsters.
lines.text: I could see them from my surveillance monitors, getting slaughtered by those... unearthly monsters.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: They're not the ones I am waiting for. Or are they?
lines.text: They're not the ones I am waiting for. Or are they?
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: [0-1.84]You seem to have a... [2.83-4.93]Unique way of speaking.
lines.text: You seem to have a... Unique way of speaking.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-1.13]And what of it? [1.67-9.57]Perhaps it is you who has an ordinary, and I dare say, uninspired, way of speaking.
lines.text: And what of it? Perhaps it is you who has an ordinary, and I dare say, uninspired, way of speaking.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: [0-4.03]Listen, we can move you someplace safe. It'd be nicer than your bunker. [4.78-7.3]More social at least.
lines.text: Listen, we can move you someplace safe. It'd be nicer than your bunker. More social at least.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-6.72]Pshaw! What fool would believe a man who offers protection against monsters? [7.47-9.55]You can not guarantee anyone's safety.
lines.text: Pshaw! What fool would believe a man who offers protection against monsters? You can not guarantee anyone's safety.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: [0-2.53]I'm not abandoning my safe haven. [3.15-5.31]And there's nothing wrong with a few traps!
lines.text: I'm not abandoning my safe haven. And there's nothing wrong with a few traps!
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: My word! Your skills are beyond measure!
lines.text: My word! Your skills are beyond measure!
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: See? I can handle the monsters.
lines.text: See? I can handle the monsters.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-1.03]I do see. [1.29-4.32]Interesting! You seem to be an oddity.
lines.text: I do see. Interesting! You seem to be an oddity.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: Are you one of the shape people?
lines.text: Are you one of the shape people?
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: Whoa, whoa, whoa. What are "shape people"?
lines.text: Whoa, whoa, whoa. What are "shape people"?
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-2.35]Shh, not so loud! [2.98-4.89]You seem not to be informed of their arrival. [5.79-8.68]Unlike myself. Hence, the fort.
lines.text: Shh, not so loud! You seem not to be informed of their arrival. Unlike myself. Hence, the fort.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: I've been called worse than an oddity.
lines.text: I've been called worse than an oddity.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [1.03-2.03]So have I. [2.7-3.7]Many a time.
lines.text: So have I. Many a time.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: [0-2.7]I could use a man of your skills. [3.64-8.96]Sadly I have become separated from my dear Granny and Olivia. [9.49-11.25]Will you return them to me?
lines.text: I could use a man of your skills. Sadly I have become separated from my dear Granny and Olivia. Will you return them to me?
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: Uh, sure, I guess I can do that.
lines.text: Uh, sure, I guess I can do that.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-7.78]Huzzah! You see, when the world began to end, I was at the gym I own when the city was besieged. [8.26-13.34]I was in such a rush to reach my fort that I left them both behind. [14.12-19.38]Granny and Olivia are all I have left in this world.
lines.text: Huzzah! You see, when the world began to end, I was at the gym I own when the city was besieged. I was in such a rush to reach my fort that I left them both behind. Granny and Olivia are all I have left in this world.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: Well, there's my brother too but we don't even talk these days.
lines.text: Well, there's my brother too but we don't even talk these days.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: I thought you wanted solitude.
lines.text: I thought you wanted solitude.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-8.74]Like my wise old Granny used to say: a family does not a man make, a man makes a family. [10.33-11.85]She came from a different time, of course.
lines.text: Like my wise old Granny used to say: a family does not a man make, a man makes a family. She came from a different time, of course.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: [0-3]I can relate. I don't have a lot of family left either. [3.25-6.01]In fact, I've been looking for my sister Jesse she--
lines.text: I can relate. I don't have a lot of family left either. In fact, I've been looking for my sister Jesse she--
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: Do not get distracted by personal drama - you're meant to aid me!
lines.text: Do not get distracted by personal drama - you're meant to aid me!
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: You own a gym?
lines.text: You own a gym?
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-4.76]Yes. I train rigorously; one has to stay fit to survive. [5.73-6.98]Does that surprise you?
lines.text: Yes. I train rigorously; one has to stay fit to survive. Does that surprise you?
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: No, you just don't sound... Nevermind.
lines.text: No, you just don't sound... Nevermind.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-2.73]Poor Granny was at home when I had to flee. [3.6-5.72]You'll find the place with ease. [6.29-12.19]It's your people that set up the "evacuation center" right next to it, after all. [13.09-16.55]I've donned my door with a trusty digital lock. [17.05-20.26]The code is 8521.
lines.text: Poor Granny was at home when I had to flee. You'll find the place with ease. It's your people that set up the "evacuation center" right next to it, after all. I've donned my door with a trusty digital lock. The code is 8521.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: 8521, got it. And Olivia?
lines.text: 8521, got it. And Olivia?
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-3.52]My sweet Olivia. [4-6.64]Like a ray of April sunshine! [7.41-8.77]She's trapped at the gym. [9.06-14.98]You'll find the place on main street -- but last I saw, it was swarming with the monsters.
lines.text: My sweet Olivia. Like a ray of April sunshine! She's trapped at the gym. You'll find the place on main street -- but last I saw, it was swarming with the monsters.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: The gym, gotcha. I'll bring them here and then we can transport you all somewhere safe.
lines.text: The gym, gotcha. I'll bring them here and then we can transport you all somewhere safe.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [1.72-6.22]Only an oddity such as the shape people could handle the monsters like that.
lines.text: Only an oddity such as the shape people could handle the monsters like that.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: I need your help reuniting me with dear Granny and my sweet Olivia.
lines.text: I need your help reuniting me with dear Granny and my sweet Olivia.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: [0-1.03]I'm back with Granny. [1.81-3.82]She isn't quite what I expected.
lines.text: I'm back with Granny. She isn't quite what I expected.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: Is she in good spirits?
lines.text: Is she in good spirits?
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: [0-2.68]All right, I'm back with Granny. [3-5.45]She's uh... quite light.
lines.text: All right, I'm back with Granny. She's uh... quite light.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [1.33-5.75]She and Olivia will have a lovely time together, I'm sure.
lines.text: She and Olivia will have a lovely time together, I'm sure.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: [0-1.67]I've got bad news. [2.68-4.95]Your... Your brother...
lines.text: I've got bad news. Your... Your brother...
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-1.75]You don't have to say it. [1.93-4.65]There's not much chance for anyone out there, is there?
lines.text: You don't have to say it. There's not much chance for anyone out there, is there?
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: [0-1.03]I just wish... [1.9-5.95]He told me he wanted to go to your "evacuation center". [6.27-9.8]He begged me to come with him, but I chose the bunker. [10.4-12.36]He must not have wanted to go without me. [12.99-15.35]Now I'm here. Alone.
lines.text: I just wish... He told me he wanted to go to your "evacuation center". He begged me to come with him, but I chose the bunker. He must not have wanted to go without me. Now I'm here. Alone.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: [0-2.01]All right, I found Olivia too. [2.65-4.95]Although, she wasn't what I thought she'd be, either.
lines.text: All right, I found Olivia too. Although, she wasn't what I thought she'd be, either.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: She can keep Granny company. Huzzah!
lines.text: She can keep Granny company. Huzzah!
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: I'm back, and I've got both Granny and Olivia with me.
lines.text: I'm back, and I've got both Granny and Olivia with me.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-2.03]What a great relief! [2.28-7.83]Thank you. Now, just carefully leave them there by the door. [8.63-11.65]I'll bring them in when it's nice and safe.
lines.text: What a great relief! Thank you. Now, just carefully leave them there by the door. I'll bring them in when it's nice and safe.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: [0-1]You know what. [1.64-4.77]I have to say, they weren't quite what I expected.
lines.text: You know what. I have to say, they weren't quite what I expected.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-2.94]That's the trouble with expectations. [3.47-5.98]One must keep an open mind!
lines.text: That's the trouble with expectations. One must keep an open mind!
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: [0-1.26]I've lost people too. [2.58-6.56]It's not easy, but you have to keep going. [7.17-8.25]That's what they'd want.
lines.text: I've lost people too. It's not easy, but you have to keep going. That's what they'd want.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0.95-2.99]That's what Granny always said.
lines.text: That's what Granny always said.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: I'm sorry.
lines.text: I'm sorry.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-1.1]It's not your fault. [1.67-3.17]I'm thankful for your help.
lines.text: It's not your fault. I'm thankful for your help.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: You could say that.
lines.text: You could say that.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: Great, excellent!
lines.text: Great, excellent!
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: When did your Granny die?
lines.text: When did your Granny die?
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: What a rude thing to insinuate about someone.
lines.text: What a rude thing to insinuate about someone.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: [0-4.05]Oh, I found something. From your brother's place. [4.59-7.71]It's a photo of him at a cabin with someone. [8.53-9.33]Is that you?
lines.text: Oh, I found something. From your brother's place. It's a photo of him at a cabin with someone. Is that you?
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-4.16]We took that photo on a hiking trip upstate. [5.06-11.35]Getting back to nature really elevates the soul -- I think he felt the same way.
lines.text: We took that photo on a hiking trip upstate. Getting back to nature really elevates the soul -- I think he felt the same way.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: You can leave it on the table for me. Thank you.
lines.text: You can leave it on the table for me. Thank you.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: [0-6.1]While I enjoy having Granny and Olivia back, it's not really... enough. [6.62-10.22]Especially with what's going on. The end of times.
lines.text: While I enjoy having Granny and Olivia back, it's not really... enough. Especially with what's going on. The end of times.
lines.speaker: SURVIVALIST

lines.text_table: [0-5.44]My brother and I had our differences, but I do miss his company. [6.14-7.48]Could you go find him? [7.96-9.01]Bring him here?
lines.text: My brother and I had our differences, but I do miss his company. Could you go find him? Bring him here?

lines.text_table: [0-2.08]Allow me to explain. [3.04-8.08]Like the Mold, Patterning also transforms matter, and beyond that, spacetime itself. [8.3-19.2]Now I have a working theory that I can use the Patterning to disrupt the Mold's operations, rendering it essentially inert.
lines.text: Allow me to explain. Like the Mold, Patterning also transforms matter, and beyond that, spacetime itself. Now I have a working theory that I can use the Patterning to disrupt the Mold's operations, rendering it essentially inert.
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: [0-4.17]I... I think your intentions are good. [4.95-6.96]And you're the expert on Mold, so... [8.04-9.04]Take the samples.
lines.text: I... I think your intentions are good. And you're the expert on Mold, so... Take the samples.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-3.05]I'm sorry, Dr. Underhill. I know you mean well, but... [3.66-5.4]I think your research is dangerous. [5.87-6.98]I have to report you.
lines.text: I'm sorry, Dr. Underhill. I know you mean well, but... I think your research is dangerous. I have to report you.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-3.09]I'm sorry, I can't let you have these samples. [3.39-4.39]It's too risky. [5.52-7.28]But I'm not going to report you, either. [7.61-9.45]I don't think you deserve to be imprisoned.
lines.text: I'm sorry, I can't let you have these samples. It's too risky. But I'm not going to report you, either. I don't think you deserve to be imprisoned.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-4.64]I can't guarantee results, but I appreciate your trust. [6.13-8.71]The Bureau, however, will be displeased.
lines.text: I can't guarantee results, but I appreciate your trust. The Bureau, however, will be displeased.
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: I have to do what I think is right. ...Don't I?
lines.text: I have to do what I think is right. ...Don't I?
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-3.04]I can't alleviate your uncertainty, Mr. Faden. [4.08-9.88]I won't be here if you return, in case you change your mind. Either way.
lines.text: I can't alleviate your uncertainty, Mr. Faden. I won't be here if you return, in case you change your mind. Either way.
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: Thank you.
lines.text: Thank you.
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: [0-1.66]I see you have become a company man. [2.17-6.72]I suppose it runs in the family. Although your sister was more of an independent thinker.
lines.text: I see you have become a company man. I suppose it runs in the family. Although your sister was more of an independent thinker.

lines.text_table: You're letting me go?
lines.text: You're letting me go?

lines.text: I guess I am.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-2.06]For your information, we are not the same. [3.64-6.16]What happens to me is not a reflection of what happened to you.
lines.text: For your information, we are not the same. What happens to me is not a reflection of what happened to you.

lines.text: Let me see the samples.

lines.text: Well, Mr. Faden? Are you going to report me to the Bureau? Or hand over my samples so I can get back to work?
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text: Excuse me -- who are you? How did you find me?
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: You're back.
lines.text: You're back.
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: [0-3.58]As I said, Patterning may be the key to stopping the Mold. [4.33-7.78]The alternative is to watch it spread across the entire planet.
lines.text: As I said, Patterning may be the key to stopping the Mold. The alternative is to watch it spread across the entire planet.
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: Your plan sounds... Iffy.
lines.text: Your plan sounds... Iffy.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: Iffy?
lines.text: Iffy?
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: [0-2.06]Maybe it is "iffy". For the moment. [3.04-7.82]More research and experimentation is needed for me to confirm my hypothesis. [8.01-10.7]But somebody needs to do something. [12.02-19]Are we so afraid of failure we would rather stand back and watch the Mold eat everything than apply our knowledge to the problem?
lines.text: Maybe it is "iffy". For the moment. More research and experimentation is needed for me to confirm my hypothesis. But somebody needs to do something. Are we so afraid of failure we would rather stand back and watch the Mold eat everything than apply our knowledge to the problem?
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: [0-3.36]The FBC already tried exploiting the Pattern with the CFD. [3.88-4.8]How'd that turn out?
lines.text: The FBC already tried exploiting the Pattern with the CFD. How'd that turn out?
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-5.12]That was a foolish man deploying untested technology against the advice of experts. [5.83-8.92]I am proposing a series of controlled experiments. [9.66-14.72]I won't pretend there are no risks, but don't lump me in with Simon Arish. [15.75-17.15]I am a scientist.
lines.text: That was a foolish man deploying untested technology against the advice of experts. I am proposing a series of controlled experiments. I won't pretend there are no risks, but don't lump me in with Simon Arish. I am a scientist.
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: I fought a Resonant that was some kind of a combination of the Mold and Patterning. Is this--
lines.text: I fought a Resonant that was some kind of a combination of the Mold and Patterning. Is this--
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-2.98]No, it's not the same at all. [4.05-8.37]That was a creature. It had agency, an objective, however alien. [9.26-15.66]What I'm talking about is a predictable biochemical process that uses Patterning to affect the structure of the Mold.
lines.text: No, it's not the same at all. That was a creature. It had agency, an objective, however alien. What I'm talking about is a predictable biochemical process that uses Patterning to affect the structure of the Mold.
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: [0-2.79]So. The decision falls on your shoulders. [4.02-9.2]Will you give me the samples and let me go to work? Or would you have me detained?
lines.text: So. The decision falls on your shoulders. Will you give me the samples and let me go to work? Or would you have me detained?
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text: That's not fair. I have no way to know how dangerous what you're proposing is. If you just explain it to them--
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text: Oh yes, I'm sure that the Bureau's famous flexibility will balance things in my favor.
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: They let me out. After everything.
lines.text: They let me out. After everything.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: And I'm sure I'll be treated exactly the same as the man with extensive paranatural abilities.
lines.text: And I'm sure I'll be treated exactly the same as the man with extensive paranatural abilities.
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: [0-1.52]You gave me no choice. [2.45-5.55]Look, you should see the Bureau psychiatrist.
lines.text: You gave me no choice. Look, you should see the Bureau psychiatrist.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-1]Call it in. [1.97-4.68]Send in the dogs. Obviously, I'm finished.
lines.text: Call it in. Send in the dogs. Obviously, I'm finished.
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: I'm sorry, I just can't--
lines.text: I'm sorry, I just can't--
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: I'm really not interested in hearing how you feel about this.
lines.text: I'm really not interested in hearing how you feel about this.
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text: If you've been moved by some assumption that you and I are alike, we're not.
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: Are you trying to talk me into detaining you?
lines.text: Are you trying to talk me into detaining you?
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: Course not.
lines.text: Course not.
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: [0-3.24]I don't know what I feel anymore. [4.62-9.74]I used to have a life, once upon a time. Now, I don't even know what...
lines.text: I don't know what I feel anymore. I used to have a life, once upon a time. Now, I don't even know what...
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: I don't know whether I should thank you or not.
lines.text: I don't know whether I should thank you or not.
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: Just... Take care of yourself.
lines.text: Just... Take care of yourself.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-1.03]I know that. [1.73-3.88]I'm doing this for you, not me.
lines.text: I know that. I'm doing this for you, not me.
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-3.55]Oh, please. I don't need your sympathy. [4.28-6.12]What I needed were those samples.
lines.text: Oh, please. I don't need your sympathy. What I needed were those samples.
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: [0-1]Leave. [1.86-5.53]You give me some privacy, in my own home. Such as it is.
lines.text: Leave. You give me some privacy, in my own home. Such as it is.
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: If you're going to be here, wouldn't you rather be useful?
lines.text: If you're going to be here, wouldn't you rather be useful?
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: [0-3.22]The FBC... Pope wants you detained. [3.97-5.64]Convince me not to listen. [6.22-7.62]How can you stop the Mold?
lines.text: The FBC... Pope wants you detained. Convince me not to listen. How can you stop the Mold?
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [2.31-4.13]"Mold" is a misnomer. [5.46-12.48]It's actually the product of extradimensional micro-organisms which consume and transform matter, [12.93-16.2]building what we see as the Mold as a colony of sorts.
lines.text: "Mold" is a misnomer. It's actually the product of extradimensional micro-organisms which consume and transform matter, building what we see as the Mold as a colony of sorts.

lines.text: You've already lost control of your research. Your "specimens" escaped your lab.

lines.text_table: They were not yet combined with the Pattern.
lines.text: They were not yet combined with the Pattern.
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text_table: But they could've been, right?
lines.text: But they could've been, right?
lines.speaker: DYLAN

lines.text_table: [0-2.77]I have been doing this work a very long time. [2.87-5.11]I know what precautions to take when.
lines.text: I have been doing this work a very long time. I know what precautions to take when.
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text: Well? If you want to watch the city be consumed, you may as well start now.

lines.text_table: What do you want?
lines.text: What do you want?
lines.speaker: UNDERHILL

lines.text: I just spent the last seven years in Lockdown with the Hiss. Anything will do. Anything.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Garcia

lines.text_table: So you got options.
lines.text: So you got options.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Pham

lines.text_table: Those Mold Clones could be useful to us.
lines.text: Those Mold Clones could be useful to us.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Garcia

lines.text_table: What’re you thinking, like a drone army?
lines.text: What’re you thinking, like a drone army?
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Pham

lines.text_table: That or a way to infiltrate the Mold, get more intel on the enemy.
lines.text: That or a way to infiltrate the Mold, get more intel on the enemy.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Garcia

lines.text_table: Both could work.
lines.text: Both could work.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Pham

lines.text_table: [0-4.22]Maybe Research should look into how those Mold clones hold up against the Hiss. [5.03-8.7]Maybe we could make a Hiss antidote from their blood. If they have blood. [8.8-13.09]And... depending on their level of awareness, obviously.
lines.text: Maybe Research should look into how those Mold clones hold up against the Hiss. Maybe we could make a Hiss antidote from their blood. If they have blood. And... depending on their level of awareness, obviously.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Garcia

lines.text_table: [0.56-3.46]Whoof. I don’t like the sound of that.
lines.text: Whoof. I don’t like the sound of that.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Pham

lines.text_table: How’s that any different from your drone army idea?
lines.text: How’s that any different from your drone army idea?
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Garcia

lines.text_table: [0.61-7.89]Well, it’s... Yeah, okay, fine. Point taken.
lines.text: Well, it’s... Yeah, okay, fine. Point taken.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Pham

lines.text_table: [0.77-4.98]Hey, you think that Threshold that chopped off all those heads is still a threat?
lines.text: Hey, you think that Threshold that chopped off all those heads is still a threat?
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Pham

lines.text_table: [0-4.97]“Chopped”? Not how I heard it described. They say the entity is dealt with. [5.44-7.73]Doesn’t mean there can’t be more of ‘em out there, though.
lines.text: “Chopped”? Not how I heard it described. They say the entity is dealt with. Doesn’t mean there can’t be more of ‘em out there, though.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Garcia

lines.text_table: Yeah, we can never really be sure, can we?
lines.text: Yeah, we can never really be sure, can we?
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Pham

lines.text_table: I guess any more bodies with missing heads will be the tip-off.
lines.text: I guess any more bodies with missing heads will be the tip-off.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Garcia

lines.text_table: [0-4.07]If you ask me, if we wanna make sure no more people lose their heads, [4.17-6.21]we should blow up the whole Threshold site.
lines.text: If you ask me, if we wanna make sure no more people lose their heads, we should blow up the whole Threshold site.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Garcia

lines.text_table: [0.58-3.64]Is that your answer to everything, explosives?
lines.text: Is that your answer to everything, explosives?
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Pham

lines.text_table: I can’t name a time explosives didn’t work out great.
lines.text: I can’t name a time explosives didn’t work out great.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Garcia

lines.text_table: [0-3.08]Well... there was that landslide in Colorado. [3.72-4.72]But that one wasn’t on me.
lines.text: Well... there was that landslide in Colorado. But that one wasn’t on me.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Garcia

lines.text_table: [0.54-1.76]What do you think of the prepper? [2.4-4.86]He finally got what he’d been waiting for all these years.
lines.text: What do you think of the prepper? He finally got what he’d been waiting for all these years.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Pham

lines.text_table: Nothing wrong with survivalism. I do take offense to the guy stealing our gear, though.
lines.text: Nothing wrong with survivalism. I do take offense to the guy stealing our gear, though.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Garcia

lines.text_table: [0-3.18]Yeah, we gotta beef up the security on our warehouses. [3.84-7.58]Somebody just walks away with our land mines and blows up our people?
lines.text: Yeah, we gotta beef up the security on our warehouses. Somebody just walks away with our land mines and blows up our people?
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Pham

lines.text_table: Fucking embarrassing.
lines.text: Fucking embarrassing.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Garcia

lines.text_table: [0.58-2.91]I’ve been thinking more about that survivalist... [3.56-7.25]If you take out the fanaticism angle... huh.
lines.text: I’ve been thinking more about that survivalist... If you take out the fanaticism angle... huh.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Pham

lines.text_table: Being ready means you don’t gotta get ready.
lines.text: Being ready means you don’t gotta get ready.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Garcia

lines.text_table: [0.65-2.97]Wish we’d been ready for this AWE.
lines.text: Wish we’d been ready for this AWE.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Pham

lines.text_table: [0-4.05]This fucking mess is beyond anything we’ve ever seen or heard of before. [4.57-6.1]The Bureau was prepared... [6.67-7.8]just not for this.
lines.text: This fucking mess is beyond anything we’ve ever seen or heard of before. The Bureau was prepared... just not for this.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Garcia

lines.text_table: [0.51-4.78]Rogers said he bumped into someone dressed in old FBC gear. [5.24-7.98]Old old, like from the original manuals.
lines.text: Rogers said he bumped into someone dressed in old FBC gear. Old old, like from the original manuals.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Garcia

lines.text_table: Are we running out of uniforms?
lines.text: Are we running out of uniforms?
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Pham

lines.text_table: The guy apparently said he was “late for everything” and hurried off.
lines.text: The guy apparently said he was “late for everything” and hurried off.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Garcia

lines.text_table: [0.62-4.61]Huh. Interesting. Fishy.
lines.text: Huh. Interesting. Fishy.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Pham

lines.text_table: Are you thinking - a mole?
lines.text: Are you thinking - a mole?
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Garcia

lines.text_table: Maybe.
lines.text: Maybe.
lines.speaker: Lw Map Ranger Pham

lines.text_table: [0.71-3.77]So, now we know what’s occurring at the Evac Site. [4.46-7.18]A heretofore unseen concentration of the Hiss. [8.26-10.99]It’s... formidable. Worrying.
lines.text: So, now we know what’s occurring at the Evac Site. A heretofore unseen concentration of the Hiss. It’s... formidable. Worrying.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0-3.28]Is it a part of the Hiss’s ongoing evolution... [3.85-9.99]or a phenomenon of its own, a centralized energy spike of sorts, feeding itself?
lines.text: Is it a part of the Hiss’s ongoing evolution... or a phenomenon of its own, a centralized energy spike of sorts, feeding itself?
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0.79-4.02]It does have many characteristics of a self-amplifying system. [5.02-14.56]I can only assume the concentration will either continue to escalate until it reaches a culmination point or, conversely, that it eventually runs out of energy and burns out.
lines.text: It does have many characteristics of a self-amplifying system. I can only assume the concentration will either continue to escalate until it reaches a culmination point or, conversely, that it eventually runs out of energy and burns out.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: I guess we’ll see.
lines.text: I guess we’ll see.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0-2.49]A shame about Clarke and Ryder. [3.82-5.43]I believe they were decent people. [6.48-11.74]Hard-working. But... I suppose they knew the risks.
lines.text: A shame about Clarke and Ryder. I believe they were decent people. Hard-working. But... I suppose they knew the risks.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0.63-5.61]Yes, yes, but I think we’re missing viable opportunities with the use of ley lines. [6.15-10.7]If we can charge the city’s power grid with paranatural energy by aligning with them, [11.25-13.45]there’s bound to be potential for much more.
lines.text: Yes, yes, but I think we’re missing viable opportunities with the use of ley lines. If we can charge the city’s power grid with paranatural energy by aligning with them, there’s bound to be potential for much more.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0-6.71]Uh-huh. Well.. our predecessors have researched that to the best of their ability back in the day. [7.77-10.29]So we have a starting point for further study, if needed.
lines.text: Uh-huh. Well.. our predecessors have researched that to the best of their ability back in the day. So we have a starting point for further study, if needed.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0-4.47]Absolutely. It wouldn’t do to overlook the efforts of those who came before us! [7.06-10.48]Speaking of, you were saying something about people?
lines.text: Absolutely. It wouldn’t do to overlook the efforts of those who came before us! Speaking of, you were saying something about people?
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: Never mind.
lines.text: Never mind.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0.6-3.75]The crew noted some interesting findings down in the subway tunnels. [4.52-7.75]Apparently, the Mold is now interacting favorably with electricity.
lines.text: The crew noted some interesting findings down in the subway tunnels. Apparently, the Mold is now interacting favorably with electricity.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0-1.73]Drawn to power, eh? [2.51-4.9]Maybe this is both symbolic and literal. [5.55-8.82]The Mold does seem to be in a state of exponential growth - [9.55-14.45]I wouldn’t be surprised to learn it’s experimenting, trying to find new stimulants, [14.87-16.95]gain more fertile ground, as it were.
lines.text: Drawn to power, eh? Maybe this is both symbolic and literal. The Mold does seem to be in a state of exponential growth - I wouldn’t be surprised to learn it’s experimenting, trying to find new stimulants, gain more fertile ground, as it were.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0.56-3.35]Sounds like you’re saying the Mold is on steroids?
lines.text: Sounds like you’re saying the Mold is on steroids?
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0-1.46]In a manner of speaking. [1.47-4.42]Now, I wouldn’t ascribe actual intelligence to it, but... [5.2-6.48]You have to wonder...
lines.text: In a manner of speaking. Now, I wouldn’t ascribe actual intelligence to it, but... You have to wonder...
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: So the Patterning is reaching downward, underground. What do we make of that?
lines.text: So the Patterning is reaching downward, underground. What do we make of that?
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0-3.34]Assuming it’s simply not filling up all available space... [3.44-9.24]um, could the subterranean environment be more beneficial for it somehow? Enclosed.
lines.text: Assuming it’s simply not filling up all available space... um, could the subterranean environment be more beneficial for it somehow? Enclosed.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0.57-2.97]Unexposed to open air. [3.55-4.85]Closer to groundwater?
lines.text: Unexposed to open air. Closer to groundwater?
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: Closer to continental drift energies?
lines.text: Closer to continental drift energies?
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: Ooh, that’s interesting.
lines.text: Ooh, that’s interesting.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0-3.25]Could the Sinkhole be just the first of many? [3.87-6.18]Is the Patterning aiming to create more of them?
lines.text: Could the Sinkhole be just the first of many? Is the Patterning aiming to create more of them?
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0.57-1.78]As in... a network? [2.26-4.27]A means of getting around faster? [4.48-7.59]Or aiming to amplify through interconnectedness?
lines.text: As in... a network? A means of getting around faster? Or aiming to amplify through interconnectedness?
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: Building from the ground up?
lines.text: Building from the ground up?
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0.76-4.02]Or the other way around, rather. Hmm.
lines.text: Or the other way around, rather. Hmm.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0-1.44]We should’ve seen this coming. [2.23-4.19]How could they be so careless? [4.71-6.27]The CFD was not ready!
lines.text: We should’ve seen this coming. How could they be so careless? The CFD was not ready!
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0.58-4.54]What else could they do? It was either that or the Hiss destroying us all.
lines.text: What else could they do? It was either that or the Hiss destroying us all.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0-2.27]We very nearly were destroyed! [2.98-8.77]This isn’t an arms race - this is supposed to be a measured response to an AWE. [8.87-13.8]Not an opportunity to come up with the most reckless paranatural weaponry imaginable. It’s...
lines.text: We very nearly were destroyed! This isn’t an arms race - this is supposed to be a measured response to an AWE. Not an opportunity to come up with the most reckless paranatural weaponry imaginable. It’s...
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0.7-2.53]You’re right about the CFD. [2.63-4.17]What’s done is done.
lines.text: You’re right about the CFD. What’s done is done.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0-1.98]I guess you were right about the Hiss. [2.72-4.33]They reached a culmination point. [5.12-9.06]Though being proven right on a theory is not as important as preventing catastrophe.
lines.text: I guess you were right about the Hiss. They reached a culmination point. Though being proven right on a theory is not as important as preventing catastrophe.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: Well...
lines.text: Well...
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0.77-5.12]We should consider the likely consequences of the CFD... event.
lines.text: We should consider the likely consequences of the CFD... event.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0.54-4.65]We can’t possibly know what is “likely” in a situation as unprecedented as this.
lines.text: We can’t possibly know what is “likely” in a situation as unprecedented as this.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0.84-4.96]True. How about “possible”? “Fathomable”?
lines.text: True. How about “possible”? “Fathomable”?
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0-6.29]Better. Anyway, I think the consequences will reveal themselves to us, whether we like it or not.
lines.text: Better. Anyway, I think the consequences will reveal themselves to us, whether we like it or not.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0.72-2.51]Aren’t we fatalistic.
lines.text: Aren’t we fatalistic.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0.57-3.1]Another tragedy resulting in fascinating data! [3.66-9.06]Terrible about the crew, of course - but this spacetime anomaly is unlike any I’ve seen before!
lines.text: Another tragedy resulting in fascinating data! Terrible about the crew, of course - but this spacetime anomaly is unlike any I’ve seen before!
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0-3.12]Is the fact that it took place underground relevant, do you think?
lines.text: Is the fact that it took place underground relevant, do you think?
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0.63-2]Could be, could be. [2.1-4.88]There are so many fantastic avenues to go down! [5.41-11.17]For instance, the different consciousnesses that exist in all of the temporal variations simultaneously... [11.57-16.48]they are able to observe themselves, but are they a part of a greater whole, [16.58-19.69]or wholly independent manifestations of the self?
lines.text: Could be, could be. There are so many fantastic avenues to go down! For instance, the different consciousnesses that exist in all of the temporal variations simultaneously... they are able to observe themselves, but are they a part of a greater whole, or wholly independent manifestations of the self?
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0-2.75]Huh. Beats me.
lines.text: Huh. Beats me.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0-3.19]What feels crucial to me about the Underpass excursion is this: [4.14-7.77]could there have been a way out of the spacetime anomaly the research team was stuck in?
lines.text: What feels crucial to me about the Underpass excursion is this: could there have been a way out of the spacetime anomaly the research team was stuck in?
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0.58-5.97]Or were they just caught in a pre-determined chain of events the moment they stepped foot in the affected area?
lines.text: Or were they just caught in a pre-determined chain of events the moment they stepped foot in the affected area?
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: I think the latter is a more merciful concept.
lines.text: I think the latter is a more merciful concept.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0.61-3.89]Remember; we’re in search of the truth, not comfort.
lines.text: Remember; we’re in search of the truth, not comfort.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0.67-5.15]Temporal paradoxes such as the Underpass anomaly are concerning, I have to admit. [5.78-10.77]If the Patterning is the cause, and if its influence is not only restricted to matter and space - [10.87-13.54]and interestingly, gravity - but also time... [14.35-17.68]We’re looking at a much vaster issue than we originally conceived.
lines.text: Temporal paradoxes such as the Underpass anomaly are concerning, I have to admit. If the Patterning is the cause, and if its influence is not only restricted to matter and space - and interestingly, gravity - but also time... We’re looking at a much vaster issue than we originally conceived.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: That is to say, we’re screwed.
lines.text: That is to say, we’re screwed.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: Your words, not mine.
lines.text: Your words, not mine.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0-1.94]It’s so obvious now! [2.39-3.91]Of course it’s a Hedron. [4.45-5.67]Of course! Haha!
lines.text: It’s so obvious now! Of course it’s a Hedron. Of course! Haha!
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0-4.22]Yes, obviously the Patterning frequency is a Hedron resonance. [4.91-6.31]It counteracts the Hiss... [7.25-8.8]and reshapes the world.
lines.text: Yes, obviously the Patterning frequency is a Hedron resonance. It counteracts the Hiss... and reshapes the world.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0.67-4.17]How long has it been on the approach? How could we not tell? [4.65-5.99]Did it cloak its presence? [6.29-7.29]Why would it? [7.5-9.49]It can’t possibly be afraid of us. [9.86-10.86]We’re nothing to it. [11.23-12.54]Less than nothing.
lines.text: How long has it been on the approach? How could we not tell? Did it cloak its presence? Why would it? It can’t possibly be afraid of us. We’re nothing to it. Less than nothing.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0-1.63]Yes. It’s not afraid. [1.86-4.23]But maybe... hindered? [5.26-8.39]And yet determined. And powerful.
lines.text: Yes. It’s not afraid. But maybe... hindered? And yet determined. And powerful.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0-1.8]The links the Hedron is trying to form with the Earth - what is their purpose? [1.8-3.27]Their mechanism? A funnel of energy, boosting it? [3.27-5.45]Or just a tether, tying the Hedron to our dimension?
lines.text: The links the Hedron is trying to form with the Earth - what is their purpose? Their mechanism? A funnel of energy, boosting it? Or just a tether, tying the Hedron to our dimension?
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: Either way, it’s a tactical weak point.
lines.text: Either way, it’s a tactical weak point.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0-3.93]So it’s... an interdimensional tug of war? [5.05-6.76]I was never much into sports.
lines.text: So it’s... an interdimensional tug of war? I was never much into sports.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0-2.5]Why did the link form here? [3.27-4.83]It’s hardly coincidental.
lines.text: Why did the link form here? It’s hardly coincidental.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0-2.54]The Oldest House is a Place of Power. [3.51-6.9]A nexus point of ley lines and paranatural energies. [7.49-9.73]And it has housed a Hedron in the past. [10.81-12.77]Is it any wonder this one would be drawn to it?
lines.text: The Oldest House is a Place of Power. A nexus point of ley lines and paranatural energies. And it has housed a Hedron in the past. Is it any wonder this one would be drawn to it?
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: Do you think the House will hold?
lines.text: Do you think the House will hold?
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0-3.42]The Oldest House has stood here for eons, in one form or another. [4.34-5.76]I’m sure it’ll survive. [6.6-7.64]Survive us, too.
lines.text: The Oldest House has stood here for eons, in one form or another. I’m sure it’ll survive. Survive us, too.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0.84-4.57]I hear a tricky old FBC protocol was activated in the Underpass. [5.47-7.86]I didn’t think load-bearing light bulbs were a thing.
lines.text: I hear a tricky old FBC protocol was activated in the Underpass. I didn’t think load-bearing light bulbs were a thing.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0-1.93]I wouldn’t put it past the Oldest House. [2.88-7.24]Regardless, the Bureau should have established an automated update system to this protocol. [7.92-10.09]Or at least kept better track of its schedule.
lines.text: I wouldn’t put it past the Oldest House. Regardless, the Bureau should have established an automated update system to this protocol. Or at least kept better track of its schedule.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0-5.07]Given that apparently the structural integrity of the entire building was -- or is -- [5.17-6.17]depending on it... [6.67-9.78]yes. Something a little off about this one.
lines.text: Given that apparently the structural integrity of the entire building was -- or is -- depending on it... yes. Something a little off about this one.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: I concur.
lines.text: I concur.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0.54-3.34]The Camera is another interesting Altered Item. [3.86-5.17]Langston must be thrilled.
lines.text: The Camera is another interesting Altered Item. Langston must be thrilled.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0.78-3.66]The folks captured by it were less than thrilled, I hear.
lines.text: The folks captured by it were less than thrilled, I hear.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0.67-2.68]It has a very localized effect. [3.15-7.39]Do we know yet if the “freezing” remains in effect indefinitely if not disrupted? [7.57-9.49]Or does it expire after a time?
lines.text: It has a very localized effect. Do we know yet if the “freezing” remains in effect indefinitely if not disrupted? Or does it expire after a time?
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0.7-2.41]That would require active testing.
lines.text: That would require active testing.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [0.6-2.89]Hmm. That’ll have to wait.
lines.text: Hmm. That’ll have to wait.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0.8-5.77]Fra Mauro’s influence on people seemed to be strangely benevolent while wholly intrusive.
lines.text: Fra Mauro’s influence on people seemed to be strangely benevolent while wholly intrusive.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0.55-2.91]I would prefer to not be brainwashed myself.
lines.text: I would prefer to not be brainwashed myself.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Caldwell

lines.text_table: [1.14-4.83]This entity’s influence worked nearly instantly through proximity. [5.31-10.26]But it was reversible. Some functional similarities to being affected by a noxious gas.
lines.text: This entity’s influence worked nearly instantly through proximity. But it was reversible. Some functional similarities to being affected by a noxious gas.
lines.speaker: Lw Oh Scientist Markson

lines.text_table: [0.92-5.53]Are you now saying Fra’s sphere of influence works on an olfactory principle?

lines.text: We’ve been told things about Director Faden’s present status. Is she actually still alive?

lines.text_table: Dylan Faden, right? The Director’s brother? Allegedly. I hope you can help me figure some things out.
lines.text: Dylan Faden, right? The Director’s brother? Allegedly. I hope you can help me figure some things out.
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: Allegedly, you are a former host (Carrier? Avatar?) of the Hiss. Is this true?
lines.text: Allegedly, you are a former host (Carrier? Avatar?) of the Hiss. Is this true?
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: The Hiss are an extradimensional resonance. Allegedly you are immune to it. Is this because of your relationship to Director Faden?
lines.text: The Hiss are an extradimensional resonance. Allegedly you are immune to it. Is this because of your relationship to Director Faden?
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: There is concern that you are “just a meat puppet” worn by the Hiss. Are you actually Dylan Faden?
lines.text: There is concern that you are “just a meat puppet” worn by the Hiss. Are you actually Dylan Faden?
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: Your file is sealed, but the word is out. Allegedly you’re responsible for the deaths of hundreds of FBC agents. Is this true?
lines.text: Your file is sealed, but the word is out. Allegedly you’re responsible for the deaths of hundreds of FBC agents. Is this true?
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: There are rumors that you are a clone of Director Trench. Is this true?
lines.text: There are rumors that you are a clone of Director Trench. Is this true?

lines.text_table: Are you loyal to the FBC?
lines.text: Are you loyal to the FBC?

lines.text_table: Is Director Trench actually dead?
lines.text: Is Director Trench actually dead?
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: The official story says Director Trench was corrupted by the Hiss. Was he actually murdered by Director Faden?
lines.text: The official story says Director Trench was corrupted by the Hiss. Was he actually murdered by Director Faden?
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: Are you actually a clone of Director Faden?
lines.text: Are you actually a clone of Director Faden?
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: The Bureau claims these Resonant entities are transformed way beyond anything with conscience or compassion. Were they ever human to begin with?
lines.text: The Bureau claims these Resonant entities are transformed way beyond anything with conscience or compassion. Were they ever human to begin with?
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: The Black Rock injectors they have distributed are supposed to protect us. Are they actually a way to control us?

lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: Is the paranatural weapon you wield influencing your actions?
lines.text: Is the paranatural weapon you wield influencing your actions?
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: Simon Arish has died as a hero. However, some data suggests otherwise. Is this a cover-up?
lines.text: Simon Arish has died as a hero. However, some data suggests otherwise. Is this a cover-up?
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: Emily Pope, formerly a minor figure, has suddenly come to a great degree of power. Has she arranged a coup?
lines.text: Emily Pope, formerly a minor figure, has suddenly come to a great degree of power. Has she arranged a coup?
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: I hear things: “We’re all that is left of humanity.” Or, “We’ve been cut out from reality.” Maybe they won’t tell us the truth to keep us from losing our minds. Is there hope for us?
lines.text: I hear things: “We’re all that is left of humanity.” Or, “We’ve been cut out from reality.” Maybe they won’t tell us the truth to keep us from losing our minds. Is there hope for us?
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: Simon Arish has allegedly been disgraced. However, some suggest he was right all along. Is this a cover-up?
lines.text: Simon Arish has allegedly been disgraced. However, some suggest he was right all along. Is this a cover-up?
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: This concludes our time together.
lines.text: This concludes our time together.
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: I didn’t expect to come out of this feeling hopeful, and perhaps that’s premature, but... maybe I’ve been letting my imagination run wild.
lines.text: I didn’t expect to come out of this feeling hopeful, and perhaps that’s premature, but... maybe I’ve been letting my imagination run wild.
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: I have a lot of concerns about what’s going on, but... it seems like on the whole, at least the threats we are facing are external, rather than internal.
lines.text: I have a lot of concerns about what’s going on, but... it seems like on the whole, at least the threats we are facing are external, rather than internal.
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: You paint a grim picture, Faden. You’re confirming a lot of the fears I’ve had.
lines.text: You paint a grim picture, Faden. You’re confirming a lot of the fears I’ve had.
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: It’s as I suspected. This organization is rotten to its core. I’ve had my concerns about it for a long time now.
lines.text: It’s as I suspected. This organization is rotten to its core. I’ve had my concerns about it for a long time now.
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: I won’t tell you who I am. Call me a concerned colleague. I’m with the FBC, and as you can tell, I have network access. Never mind how.
lines.text: I won’t tell you who I am. Call me a concerned colleague. I’m with the FBC, and as you can tell, I have network access. Never mind how.
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: I have a lot of concerns, and questions about recent events. You are in a unique position to answer them.
lines.text: I have a lot of concerns, and questions about recent events. You are in a unique position to answer them.
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: I have to keep this very simple. So your ability to answer will be limited. However, I have other sources of intel and will be cross-checking.
lines.text: I have to keep this very simple. So your ability to answer will be limited. However, I have other sources of intel and will be cross-checking.
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: You can participate or not participate. If you say you’re done talking, we’re finished. But I’m hoping you’ll help me find out what’s REALLY going on.
lines.text: You can participate or not participate. If you say you’re done talking, we’re finished. But I’m hoping you’ll help me find out what’s REALLY going on.
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: The nature of our organization breeds paranoia and uncertainty, and uncertainty leads to anxiety.
lines.text: The nature of our organization breeds paranoia and uncertainty, and uncertainty leads to anxiety.
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: You have soothed mine. Keep doing what you’re doing, Dylan.
lines.text: You have soothed mine. Keep doing what you’re doing, Dylan.
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: I suppose we’ll see how things turn out. Stay safe out there, Faden.
lines.text: I suppose we’ll see how things turn out. Stay safe out there, Faden.
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: I don’t know if I am encouraged, exactly, but... perhaps things aren’t as bad as I thought.
lines.text: I don’t know if I am encouraged, exactly, but... perhaps things aren’t as bad as I thought.
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: Or are you an active part of it? Give me time. I’ll figure it out. They (you?) won’t get away with it.
lines.text: Or are you an active part of it? Give me time. I’ll figure it out. They (you?) won’t get away with it.
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: You’re a part of the problem, of course, but I can’t figure out how you fit in, exactly. Are you just caught up in this?
lines.text: You’re a part of the problem, of course, but I can’t figure out how you fit in, exactly. Are you just caught up in this?
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: You’re trying to destabilize everything, aren’t you? I see you for what you are, Faden. I see you.
lines.text: You’re trying to destabilize everything, aren’t you? I see you for what you are, Faden. I see you.
lines.speaker: FBC TERMINAL

lines.text_table: The only reason I’m not doing everything I can to tear it all down yet is because ultimately, I can’t just take your word for it.
